resources.string: Choose Create New Project, enter a name, pick Empty, Office, Residential or Data center, then choose display units. Templates provide a starting level, drawing layers and room footprints. The drawing canvas opens after creation. Project details lets you change the name, description and units.

Open Draw and choose a shape. Choosing a tool creates nothing: its highlight, hint and translucent preview show what will be placed. Precision pointer is on by default. Touch and drag to aim the crosshair away from your finger; lifting leaves it in place. Tap Place to confirm each point, or use the four nudge arrows first. Sized shapes use the dimensions displayed in project units: a rectangle or ellipse starts at 1 m by 1 m and a circle at 1 m diameter. Enable Draw by points for opposite-corner rectangles, centre/radius circles, centre/radii ellipses, three-corner triangles or a polygon from picked points. Line takes two confirmed endpoints; Arc takes a start, a point on the arc, then an end. For a polyline or spline, confirm points and choose Done. The selected level supplies the default floor. Cancel discards unfinished points. Completion shows Placed, selects the object and returns to Select. Enable Keep tool active after placing in Settings for repeated placement.

Choose Text, enter its lettering and height in Tools, aim its insertion point, then tap Place. Leader takes an arrow point and bends, then Done. An aligned dimension takes two measured endpoints and a label point. Angular takes the vertex, first arm, second arm, then label position. Radial takes the centre, radius point, then label position. Confirm each point with Place; lifting your finger does not add one. These drawing dimensions keep fixed anchors. Use Dimension from reference to link a measurement to another object. Turning Precision pointer off in Settings restores direct canvas taps.

Choose a primitive, review its dimensions in Tools, aim the translucent preview with the precision crosshair, then tap Place. A box starts as a 1 m cube; a sphere has a 0.5 m radius. Cylinder and cone start with a 1 m diameter and 1 m height; pyramid starts with a 1 m square base and 1 m height. Values display in current units, such as 1000 mm for 1 m. Enable Draw by points to confirm a base or radius instead. The active level supplies the default floor; snapped 3D points can retain their actual elevation. Solid height extends upward and a sphere extends above and below its centre. Tap a view cube face or corner to inspect the object and choose a display mode in View.

Choose Select and tap an object; tap empty canvas to deselect. The floating toolbar offers Move/Rotate, Copy, Delete, Properties and More. Properties opens only when you tap it. In Move mode, drag the centre square with four arrows to move on ground X/Y without changing height. Red X, green Y and blue Z arrows move along one axis, including raising and lowering with Z. Snapping stays active and every move handle has a finger-sized target, including when an axis points into the view. Switch to Rotate for red X, green Y and blue Z bands: X/Y tilt and Z turns flat. The current angle appears while dragging. More → Rotation snap offers 1°, 5°, 15°, 45° or 90°; the default is 15°. More → Scale reveals W/D sides, base corners and the separate H height handle. Keep width/depth proportions locks a corner’s ratio. Properties edits X/Y/Z, Rotation X/Y/Z and the same local width/depth/height in project units. Flat axes cannot gain thickness. Body dragging navigates by default; Settings can enable moving selected bodies.

Open View to choose Wireframe, Hidden Line, Shaded, Shaded with Edges, X-ray or Realistic. Closed geometry uses object, system or material colours and simple lighting. The mode is remembered with the project and applies to plan and orbit views. Layers has layer/system checkboxes and measurement visibility. Drag the top-left view cube to orbit, tap a face to align, or tap a corner for isometric. Long press the cube for Plan 2D, Perspective or Orthographic. Home beside it restores the isometric orthographic view and fits the drawing. Zoom extents is in View. The gizmo hides during camera orbiting. Hide panels keeps the bottom status bar; Show panels restores the controls.

Open Measure and choose Measure distance, then aim and confirm two points with Place. Touching, dragging or lifting only adjusts the pending crosshair. A live distance from the first confirmed point helps aim the second. The default saved readout shows distance only. Enable Show detailed measurement (angle and coordinates) in Settings to reveal horizontal PLAN distance, angles and X/Y/Z for saved measurements too. Dimension from reference takes a confirmed object, a wall corner, another object or a visible grid line, then a confirmed label point. Components use their insertion position. Detailed AFFL reports height above the source level’s floor when available. Saved measurements lets you edit the name, points, label and readouts, hide them or delete them. Object references update when their hosts move. PNG or PDF in View includes visible dimensions and the current detail preference without editor handles or the precision overlay.

With a selection, use Copy or Delete in the floating toolbar. More contains Paste, Mirror X/Y, Array, layer, colour, lock, Rotate 90°, Undo and Redo. Scale handles appear only after choosing Scale. Arrays include the original cell, allow negative X/Y spacing, and accept 2–1,000 cells with up to 100 rows and columns; a repeated axis needs nonzero spacing. While a tool is unfinished, Undo/Redo restores its confirmed draft points and nudge adjustments. A completed placement, handle drag or array is one document undo step. Undo/Redo also covers object colour/layer/lock, canvas project settings and layer/system visibility. Camera navigation and panel opening do not add document undo steps. History is bounded by Settings and stays in the current editing session; reopening starts a new history and clipboard. Save keeps the resulting drawing.

Save writes your project to the local library on this device. Export creates a portable .eezydraw file in a location you choose. If you select a save folder in Settings, the app also writes project copies there; the local library stays available on this device.

Continue Project opens the most recent project. Select a recent-project thumbnail to open that project instead. Open from file imports a .eezydraw file into your local library. Existing local projects are not silently overwritten by imported files.

Settings controls defaults for newly created projects. Changing a project’s display units does not rescale its geometry: stored lengths stay in metres. Existing projects keep their own units and project settings. Theme, input mode and other app preferences are stored separately from project files. Precision pointer is on by default. Set its 80dp offset distance, right-handed above-left or left-handed above-right side, magnifier on/off and 2×–4× zoom, project-grid or custom nudge step, and snap haptic feedback. Switch Precision pointer off for direct-tap placement. Stylus input uses the pen tip without the finger offset, while Place still confirms the point.

Choose an autosave interval in Settings, or switch it off. Autosave runs silently while you keep drawing. Show autosave notification is off by default; enable it to receive a success message. Saving failures remain visible. Explicit Save still confirms success. With backups enabled, saving retains the preceding saved version. If a project cannot be read, use the offered backup recovery action to restore an available earlier version.

Open a project and choose a tool from Draw, Edit, View, Measure or Library. Follow the hint and preview, touch or drag to aim, then tap Place to confirm each point. Selection controls appear beside the selected object.

Tap a card or button to open it. Swipe vertically to scroll forms and recent projects. Tap a text field to edit it. Use the back arrow or Android Back to return; save any changes before leaving a project.

In Select mode, drag the plan with one finger to pan and pinch to zoom. With a point-picking tool active, a finger controls an offset crosshair connected by a thin line. The offset flips near canvas edges. Drag to adjust, lift to leave the target, use nudge arrows for exact steps, and tap the large Place button to confirm. A 120dp loupe magnifies the target at 2×–4× while dragging and moves to a clear corner. Snap markers and labels identify endpoint, midpoint, intersection, perpendicular, grid or wall-edge targets; Settings can disable snap haptics. A live distance appears after the first confirmed point. A stylus uses its tip without the offset but still requires Place. Precision pointer off restores direct taps. Done finishes a valid multi-point construction; Cancel discards it. Tap an object to select it or empty canvas to deselect. Move uses the ground X/Y centre square and red X, green Y and blue Z arrows. Rotate shows three axis bands; Scale is in More. Body dragging navigates unless enabled in Settings. In 3D, drag to orbit or use two fingers to pan and zoom. Drag the cube to orbit, tap faces to align, tap corners for isometric and use Home to reset. Zoom window fits a rectangle; Zoom extents fits the visible drawing.

On the canvas, use Ctrl+C to copy, Ctrl+V to paste, Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo, and Delete to remove the selection. Escape cancels an unfinished drawing operation or clears selection. Use Tab to move between controls, Enter or Space to activate a focused button, and Android Back to return. TalkBack announces labelled controls and transform-handle actions. Keyboard editing shortcuts apply when the canvas has focus; text fields keep their normal editing behavior.

EEZY DRAW is a tablet-first MEP drawing application. This version includes project creation, a local library, portable project files, settings, help, plan and orbit views with six display modes, shared precision pointing, saved reference measurements, PNG/PDF sharing, shape and annotation tools, 3D primitives, selection, transforms and session undo/redo. Coordination engines and external CAD file codecs remain separate development stages.

The project library works offline. Exports and save-folder copies go only to the locations you choose. Uninstalling the app removes its private library; keep exported copies of important projects. Feedback does not attach project files.
Tell us what happened, what you expected, or what would make EEZY DRAW more useful.
You choose the app and recipient. Nothing is sent automatically, and project files are not attached.
